A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete text, equations, tables, and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across the reorganization.

before.justification: Section 5 reports four original Lending Club experiments. Table 1 gives confidence intervals for the frequency of ecosystem fairness worsening after individual fairness adjustment.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C retain those experiments and report additional Adult, independently sampled training, and three-classifier experiments, together with harm-magnitude results.

M1.justification: The classifier training and Fairlearn fairness-adjustment approach are retained; no new learning or postprocessing algorithm is proposed. Revised fairness definitions are theoretical changes, while random forests enter as components of additional evaluation configurations.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates only Lending Club loan repayment prediction, using mortgage status as the protected attribute. v2 adds Adult Census Income prediction above $50,000, with gender as the protected attribute, substantially extending the evaluated population, prediction task, and domain.

E2.justification: Both versions compare ecosystems before and after the same fairness adjustment; no alternative mitigation baseline is introduced. The added random forests serve as ecosystem participants in three-classifier experiments, rather than comparison methods against a proposed algorithm.

E3.justification: The original experiments retain their stated settings. Appendix C adds independently sampled training sets, three-classifier configurations, and Adult experiments with White/non-White training partitions. It also introduces the after/before EOC ratio, conditional on worsening, as an additional evaluation measure.

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses of how large fairness deterioration is when it occurs, and tests its persistence under independent training samples and three-classifier competition (Appendix C.1, C.3, and C.5). These substantially extend the earlier prevalence analysis. The different-borrower-subsets experiment in C.2 already existed in v1.

E5.justification: Both versions state 500 repetitions per training size for Experiments 1–3 and report standard errors and 95% confidence intervals. The added tables extend the existing uncertainty-reporting practice to additional outcomes; no changed run count, seed disclosure, or new inference procedure is stated.

E6.justification: All four original likelihood-CI rows are preserved in v2 Tables 1 and 3. Tables 2 and 4–12 add conditional effect sizes and results for the additional experiments. Section 5 also changes the reported 100k harm frequencies for Experiments 1 and 2 from 30.0% and 15.6% to 30.1% and 15.8%, despite retaining their confidence intervals.

T1.justification: Section 2 replaces unconditional WE/WEC welfare definitions with v-EO/v-EOC definitions conditioned on Y=1, a substantive mathematical revision. Appendix B adds EDC/DPC definitions and corresponding bounds and derivations. The utility and multiple-lender extensions now in Sections 3.1.1–3.1.2 already appeared in v1 Appendix A.

C1.justification: The abstract's central claims—that individually fair classifiers can produce unfair ecosystems and fairness adjustment can worsen ecosystem fairness—remain unchanged. The introduction and discussion add explicit claims covering Equalized Odds and Demographic Parity, while the introduction removes the explicit first-paper assertion.

C2.justification: The discussion adds a regulatory tradeoff between ecosystem fairness and competition benefits, and specifies remaining utility-model limitations. Appendix C.2 newly characterizes the subset experiment's harm magnitude as small. Appendix B.2.1 also adds an incorrect explanation that increasingly accurate DP classifiers have correlations approaching zero; perfect nonconstant classifiers instead have correlation one.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository pointer in Section 5 and documents the Adult prediction target, input features, and protected attribute in Appendix C.4. The existing Fairlearn reference and approximate home-computer runtime disclosure are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Bower et al. (2017) and Dwork and Ilvento (2019), acknowledging their prior insight that individual classifier fairness need not compose. It replaces v1's broad priority positioning with distinctions based on decentralized competition, parallel decisions, correlations, and quantified unfairness. This substantively revises the relationship to the closest prior research.

P1.justification: Proofs are consolidated into Appendix A, while the earlier appendix's utility and multiple-lender extensions move into Section 3. Experiment 4 moves to Appendix C. The model, related-work discussion, contribution roadmap, and concluding discussion are substantially reorganized or rewritten.

P2.justification: The document adopts a substantially denser conference layout with redesigned title and author blocks and different typography. v1's four-row Table 1 is split between v2 Tables 1 and 3, and ten additional tables present effect sizes and new experiments.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the evidence beyond v1's single-dataset harm frequencies through Adult results, conditional harm magnitudes, and independent-training and three-classifier checks. It also acknowledges important prior composition research. Conditioning welfare on Y=1 resolves the mismatch between v1's unconditional welfare definition and EO. The new claim that near-perfect classifiers' correlations vanish is incorrect, but this localized explanatory flaw does not outweigh the empirical, definitional, and positioning gains.
